stemMd: A laboratory has the rule: if a sample is contaminated, it is isolated or destroyed, or both. A sample is neither isolated nor destroyed. What follows?

options.label: A
options.textMd: It was isolated and then destroyed.

options.label: B
options.textMd: It is contaminated but exempt from the rule.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Every uncontaminated sample is neither isolated nor destroyed.

options.label: E
options.textMd: It must be the only sample in the laboratory.

explanationMd: The consequent is an inclusive disjunction. Neither outcome makes that consequent false, so contraposition rules out contamination. This does not establish the converse for every uncontaminated sample.

distractorRationale.a: That conflicts with the stated absence of both outcomes.
distractorRationale.d: This reverses the implication and is not established.

independentSolve.workingNotes: Blind re-solve in the 5 November 2026 AI audit of this expansion (the review packet held no key, explanation or distractor notes; status "key_matched"; it checked for competing defensible answers and flagged none): Contamination implies isolated-or-destroyed; neither means uncontaminated.
